how: Members repeatedly solicit builders for named sprites, lettering, and further projects, while a later switch of effort shows that a call need not secure its proposed object.
Limited room constrains the Guide attempt and makes replacing an adjacent flag depend on having enough people.
A named participant begins the sword at a specified hilt coordinate and others later report completion.
Builders debate recognizable Terraria imagery, border appearance, and which drawing to finish first.
Participants report the Guide halfway complete and then finished, providing textual uptake beyond the initial appeal.
Anchor coordinates and a posted lettering template direct shared work, although the template is circulated before its location is settled.
Browser scripts maintain the Guide and require revisions around neighbours, while later participants dispute scripting and admit using it despite disapproval.

Treat this room as a local exception to undecided organization because one builder explicitly suspends placements pending votes or suggestions, without establishing a permanent leader or formal election.
Negotiated accommodation depends on circulating current templates and adapting running scripts, since stale programs can make collaborators fight their own changes.
Participants hand curation over before sleep, rally repairs, and harden visibility through embedding and borders.
A neighbour identifies damage to its outline and the responsible participant recognizes the mistake and offers replacement tiles.
Participants avoid completed neighbouring work, explain why they do not want to destroy another picture, and apologise for mistaken damage.
Negotiations change overlapping sword colours, arrange a construct move, and revise the Enterprise template so neighbouring pictures can coexist.
Neighbouring groups offer defence and trade assistance moving one construct for help building another.
Members relay an invitation into another group's chat and report negotiations that secured a revised neighbouring template.
Requests for space and hoped-for protection establish guest seeking, but they do not establish accepted residence under a host's approval authority.
A two-room agreement exchanges assistance through a shared negotiation channel, supporting the smallest coalition form rather than a continuing multiroom organization.
Loss prompts requests for a replacement site and an explicit choice between restoring the Guide where it stood and moving elsewhere.
After destruction, participants can rebuild at the contested site before making a smaller neighbour-accommodating adjustment, so recovery need not begin with abandoning the old location.
Template conflicts show difficulty implementing agreements, while the coded negotiation never establishes a dispute over who may bind the room.
A retrospective narrator briefly retells canvas damage using the game's corruption vocabulary, giving the event a fandom idiom without establishing a pre-existing quarrel.
The rival is named through damage to the sword rather than an evidenced pre-canvas dispute, leaving any prior quarrel unobserved.
The retaliation proposal names the lost sword as its grievance and supplies no evidence of an inherited tie selecting the rival.
False release and cancellation claims are exposed through date recognition and admissions of being fooled.
Locate the rotating game takeover in the community's Discord rather than attributing that takeover to the subreddit itself.
Suspected April Fools interference becomes practical troubleshooting when participants reset controls and identify a mod as the source.
A joke can license a substantive grievance that develops into an argument about obligations and unequal treatment independently of canvas organizing.
statement: using an April Fools joke to press a substantive grievance

how: Promoting a template through a new post and debating scripts do not establish moderator containment or a host-wide boundary around canvas talk.
Completion announcements, thanks, and pride in a single eye mark both collective work and an individual's contribution.
Participants mark closure, mourn unfinished projects, and recount how restoration and a neighbour-driven move produced the final double-headed Guide.
Recording begins during placement when maintaining the completed Guide is explicitly directed toward securing a subreddit snapshot.
One member invites others to a Guide rebuild and two surviving titles claim solo sword rebuilds, supporting individual continuation rather than demonstrated collective migration.
The final Guide is explained and defended as evidence of cooperation, but a contest over which cleaned or corrected version should be retained remains unobserved.
A participant proposes retaliatory expansion into a larger sword, establishing an attack-oriented call without demonstrating that an attack was carried out.
Retrospective blame names the sword's destroyers, while another participant admits manual help on the damaging work and apologises.
A brief collective completion report and thanks appear without asking anything back.
The Guide appeal receives progress and completion reports, supporting answered recruitment while leaving the identities and actions of silent placers unknown.
The same starter combines a call with a first placed anchor, so starting and recruitment are bundled rather than separately timed stages.
A completion declaration is directly answered by a request to keep the finished Guide intact for a snapshot.
A defender explicitly describes reversing overlapping pixels before reaching an agreement to recolour the hilt and preserve both drawings.
Restraint may motivate a treaty request before any settled border exists, so an agreement cannot be required as the source of every decision to spare neighbours.
A stated wish to preserve another group's representation motivates seeking a peace treaty before boundary settlement.
Script adoption follows restoration pressure and practical availability, but the coded passages do not establish timer-limited manpower exhaustion as the sufficient cause.
Progress reporting culminates in a collective completion declaration and thanks for the shared work.
The Guide's completion directly prompts maintenance for a screenshot and an answering report that snapshots were taken.
Recording and off-site rebuilding both occur, but the continuation invitation does not say that a record caused the decision to rebuild.
Perceived crowding can coexist with restoration at the current site, so insufficient space does not by itself establish cessation of defence or relocation.
A lettering template is posted while its location remains unsettled, so template circulation cannot be treated as proof that the whole shared plan is agreed.
Brief acceptances and reciprocal promises are visible, but these exchanges cannot establish that joining is preferred or that silent placers experience an obligation to answer.
A threat thread receives an outside offer of defence, although the offer alone does not measure shortage of hands or completed assistance.
Negotiation over occupied space yields a reported bargain to move one group's work with assistance and receive help building the logo.
The retaliatory call explicitly answers the sword's destruction, so recruitment alone does not explain why the rival becomes an attack target.
Restraint elsewhere cannot establish an answer refusing this particular retaliatory proposal, whose coded record supplies no such response.
The peace-treaty exchange concerns a separate overlap and cannot be treated as the outcome of the sword retaliation call.
Retaliation and later blame share a rival, but no coded passage makes the retaliation proposal the cause of the retrospective blame.
The reciprocal logo bargain and outside defence offer do not establish that upkeep pressure caused coalition formation.
Repeated calls and a choice to publicise a template provide no observed containment response to a canvas-post flood.
A negotiation and stale-script warning do not establish that making an agreement prompted a dispute about who may commit the room.
